---
title: "Plant physiology"
---

Plants acquire resources, build organs and respond to their surroundings while
remaining rooted in place. Follow a leaf from its construction through transport
and metabolism to development, defence and biotechnology.

This first teaching draft supplies explanations and classroom investigations.
Departmental laboratory protocols and formal assessment instructions remain
separate. No programming is required.

| Unit | Guiding question | Study route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1. Organisation | How does a plant build a functioning body? | [Read](organisation/index.qmd), [slides](organisation/lec.qmd), [exercise](organisation/exercise.qmd), [self-check](organisation/quiz.qmd) |
| P2. Water and nutrition | How do resources enter and move through a plant? | [Read](water-nutrition/index.qmd), [slides](water-nutrition/lec.qmd), [exercise](water-nutrition/exercise.qmd), [self-check](water-nutrition/quiz.qmd) |
| P3. Carbon and metabolism | How does captured light support the whole organism? | [Read](carbon-metabolism/index.qmd), [slides](carbon-metabolism/lec.qmd), [exercise](carbon-metabolism/exercise.qmd), [self-check](carbon-metabolism/quiz.qmd) |
| P4. Development | How does a signal change growth and reproduction? | [Read](development/index.qmd), [slides](development/lec.qmd), [exercise](development/exercise.qmd), [self-check](development/quiz.qmd) |
| P5. Stress and biotechnology | How can physiology inform an intervention? | [Read](stress-biotechnology/index.qmd), [slides](stress-biotechnology/lec.qmd), [exercise](stress-biotechnology/exercise.qmd), [self-check](stress-biotechnology/quiz.qmd) |

Draw compartments, label movement and predict what changes if one step is
disrupted. Invented exercise observations are labelled as teaching examples;
they do not reproduce an actual experiment's results. Use the reading, then the
short lecture deck, then exercises and self-checks. A scientific explanation
needs a mechanism and evidence, not just a named hormone or pathway.
